healthcareSystem: Universal (Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia — NFZ). EU citizens covered by EHIC. All others pay out-of-pocket or via travel insurance.
qualityNotes: Good quality healthcare, particularly in Warsaw, Kraków, and other major cities. Major cities have modern hospitals with increasing English-speaking staff. Rural areas may have fewer English-speaking doctors and older facilities. Private healthcare is affordable and widely available in cities.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open Mon-Fri 8am-6pm, Sat 8am-3pm. Some 24/7 pharmacies in major cities. Look for 'Apteka' signs — green cross.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacists in tourist areas and major cities often speak English. Many common OTC medications are available. EU prescriptions are accepted. Poland has strong generic medication availability. Pharmacies in Poland can compound custom medications.
prescriptionRules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Prescriptions from outside the EU require a Polish doctor to re-issue them. Some medications available by prescription in other countries may be OTC in Poland.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires prescription in Poland. Small personal-use quantities may be brought with proper documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription or doctor consultation. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. EU regulations apply. Carry doctor's letter and original prescription and packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin) and ADHD stimulants
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires documentation and possibly special permission. Contact Polish health authorities if traveling with ADHD medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal for recreational use. Medical cannabis is legal but strictly regulated. CBD products with no THC are legal and widely available.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Polish or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry original prescriptions and multilingual medical certificates.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required but strongly recommended for all travelers.
travelInsurance.tips: Poland is very affordable for healthcare — doctor visits, dental care, and medications cost a fraction of Western Europe. Travel insurance is still essential for emergencies and medical evacuation. Private clinics in major cities accept international insurance and have English-speaking staff.

recommended: tick-borne encephalitis (if hiking in forested eastern regions)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Eastern Poland has tick-borne encephalitis risk in forested areas during summer months.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Poland. Polish tap water meets EU standards and is regularly tested.
foodSafetyTips: Poland has good food safety standards. Traditional dishes like pierogi, bigos, żurek, and kielbasa are generally safe. Bigos (hunter's stew) is famously hardy and safe. Polish dairy (oscypek, bundz) at mountain stands is generally safe. Avoid unpasteurized milk from unregulated sources.
medicalTourismNote: Poland is a growing medical tourism destination — especially dental care, cosmetic surgery, and orthopedic procedures. Costs are significantly lower than Western Europe while quality is good, particularly in Kraków and Warsaw.
metaDescription: Health & medication guide for Poland. Emergency numbers (112/999/997/998), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance advice, and vaccination recommendations.

hospitals.name: Medicover Hospital
hospitals.notes: International private hospital chain. English widely spoken.

hospitals.name: University Hospital Kraków
hospitals.notes: Major university hospital near tourist center.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care at affordable prices. Poland is a dental tourism destination.
dentalCare.costRange: PLN 100-250 ($25-60) for consultation; PLN 150-400 ($35-95) for fillings
dentalCare.notes: Poland offers quality dental care at 50-70% less than Western Europe. Kraków and Warsaw have clinics catering to tourists.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies.

mentalHealth.notes: English mental health services in major cities. Private therapy: PLN 150-350 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Poland has been improving accessibility. Modern areas are accessible. Historic old towns can be challenging.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Warsaw and Kraków have accessible trams and buses. PKP trains offer assistance.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Kraków's Old Town is largely flat and manageable. Auschwitz-Birkenau memorial has wheelchair access. Wieliczka Salt Mine has limited accessibility.

insuranceClaimProcess: EU citizens with EHIC access public emergency care. Private clinics accept international insurance. Keep all rachunki (receipts) and documentation.
